verification.runtime_check: Booted the FastAPI app under uvicorn with Redis and Postgres URLs pointing at closed ports. /health returned ok; created a price_above rule via REST; two real websocket browser clients subscribed; fake upstream pushed trade frames; verified fan-out, edge-triggered single signed webhook, ref-counted single upstream subscribe/unsubscribe, disconnect cleanup, upstream drop/reconnect/resubscribe, and clean shutdown.

bug.description: With Redis unreachable, each browser subscribe blocks the websocket handler for the redis socket timeout (about 2s) in cache.get_price, so later control messages on that socket, including disconnect cleanup of an in-flight handler, are delayed and the upstream unsubscribe lagged ~2s+. Functionally correct but slow degradation; ticks are unaffected.
bug.reproduction: Run app with REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:1/0, connect a ws client, send subscribe then close immediately; upstream unsubscribe arrives only after the redis timeout (scratchpad e2e.py with sleep 0.5 after b.close()).

verification.self_critique: Not tested: real Redis, real asyncpg/TimescaleDB (SQL, hypertable creation, persistence reload), real Finnhub framing/auth, docker-compose up, GitHub Actions execution, a real browser. Fake upstream was a local websockets server, which is more faithful than the in-process stub but still not Finnhub. Python 3.13 locally vs 3.12 in CI. CI runs pytest with DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL set to live service containers, a path not exercised here. Percent-change rule only covered by pytest, not e2e.
